query: If teams adopted the goal-management practices described by top performers, how much would achievement improve?

per_column.name: performance_category
per_column.rationale: A binned recoding of percent_complete/achievement level itself (At Risk, Underperformer, Top Performer). It is a discretization of the outcome, not an intervenable treatment. The query's treatment is 'adopting goal-management practices described by top performers'; this column merely labels who is a top performer rather than encoding the practices as a settable lever.

per_column.name: achievement_gap
per_column.rationale: Difference between target and actual completion, a direct transform of the outcome (percent_complete vs target_percentage). Not a common cause of a treatment; it is a restatement of the outcome/gap.

per_column.name: target_alignment
per_column.rationale: Alignment of achievement to target (Misaligned/Exceeded/Well Aligned) is downstream of both target-setting and actual completion; it is a function of the outcome relative to target_percentage rather than a confounding common cause. It is not an intervenable practice lever.

per_column.name: improvement_potential
per_column.rationale: Deterministically keyed to performance_category (each category maps to a single value), so it is a derived estimate attached to the outcome bins, not an intervenable treatment nor a confounder. It presupposes the effect rather than setting up an interventional comparison.

judge.rationale: The query poses a genuine what-if: intervening on teams' adoption of specific goal-management practices and measuring the effect on achievement (percent_complete). A valid answer requires (a) a treatment encoding the intervenable practices top performers use (e.g., cadence of check-ins, milestone decomposition, target-setting method) that an actor could set, and (b) confounders that are common causes of both practice adoption and achievement (e.g., department resourcing, team capacity, priority/leadership support) — ideally ones not already in the query. None of the added columns supply an intervenable treatment: they are all recodings or transforms of the outcome and its target gap (performance_category, achievement_gap, target_alignment, improvement_potential). improvement_potential even hard-codes an effect estimate per outcome bin, circularly assuming the answer. No confounders are provided at all. The set fails the interventional test.
